mechanism_narrative: The four-week downward momentum in RETAIL_REC (from -13.3 to -17.9) and the steady rise in GROCERY_PHARM (8.1 to 9.6) show spending shifting from discretionary retail to essentials; this substitution continues and keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite the current downward RETAIL_REC and rising GROCERY_PHARM pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A weekly RETAIL_REC print below -17.0 acts as a threshold breach that signals accelerated avoidance of discretionary venues; once breached, TRANSIT remains depressed and pulls RETAIL_REC further below its recent mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls below -17.0 in any week
failure_condition: After a RETAIL_REC print below -17.0, the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of GROCERY_PHARM above 9, PARKS below 5, and RESIDENTIAL above 3.5 marks a home-centered nesting regime; errands consolidate near home and discretionary retail trips are deferred, lowering RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM > 9, PARKS < 5, and RESIDENTIAL > 3.5 jointly hold, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT below -20 and WORKPLACES below -8 with RESIDENTIAL above 3.5 indicate policy-driven containment; retail and recreation venues face reduced footfall and RETAIL_REC stays lower over four weeks.
failure_condition: Under a tightening-restrictions regime with TRANSIT < -20 and WORKPLACES < -8, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than its prior 28-day mean.
